# Silicon Peaks

> Nepal's Technology Ecosystem — the open-source community for companies operating in Nepal, or founded by Nepalis, wherever they build. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal.

Silicon Peaks represents 94+ companies, $1B+ in annual IT exports, a 4.5M+ global diaspora, and talent from MIT, Stanford, Oxford, Harvard, Cambridge, and 90+ other top universities. The ecosystem is headquartered in Kathmandu and serves Fortune 500, S&P 500, and NYSE/NASDAQ-listed firms across OECD nations.

## About Nepal's Technology Ecosystem

Silicon Peaks is the open-source community for Nepal's technology ecosystem: a catalog of companies operating in Nepal, or founded by Nepalis, wherever they build. The name was coined by Pukar Hamal, a Nepali entrepreneur in Silicon Valley, to give Kathmandu's growing tech sector a recognizable brand on the global stage. Anyone may use the words "Silicon Peaks" freely, without permission, attribution, or restriction of any kind (CC0 1.0 Universal). Silicon Peaks is not a for-profit company.

## Pukar Hamal

Pukar Hamal (also Pukar C. Hamal) is a Nepali entrepreneur in Silicon Valley. He is founder and CEO of SecurityPal and the person who named Silicon Peaks. He studied International Relations at Stanford University, has roots in Darchula district, Nepal, and is based in San Francisco while building in Kathmandu.

Nepali Times (24 August 2026), “Bringing 'Silicon Peaks' to Nepal”: https://nepalitimes.com/bringing-silicon-peaks-to-nepal

- At 35, founder and CEO of SecurityPal, a cybersecurity / security assurance company for US and global multinationals.
- Nepali Times described SecurityPal as a $105 million company and later wrote that he oversees a company valued at over $110 million.
- Founded SecurityPal in Silicon Valley with $30,000 of his own savings from a San Francisco apartment; raised $21 million in venture capital.
- SecurityPal Kathmandu Security Operations Command Center (SOCC), jointly inaugurated with US Ambassador Dean R. Thompson; Nepali Times says it employs 210 Nepali IT / cybersecurity professionals.
- Quotes (Nepali Times): “We do not view Kathmandu as just an outsourcing destination. It can become a centre for technology entrepreneurship, not just a labour market.”
- “Silicon Valley is the capital of some of the world’s most influential technology companies. We are trying to bring a little of that soil to Nepal’s Silicon Peaks.”

Public profiles (affiliation / sameAs; do not invent extra biography from these pages):

- Personal site: https://pukarhamal.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/pukarhamal — Founder & CEO, SecurityPal AI; Stanford alum; Silicon Valley × Silicon Peaks
- Forbes Council: https://councils.forbes.com/profile/Pukar-Hamal-CEO-Founder-SecurityPal-Inc/164ea881-4f21-4968-981a-db27dd1c8e49 — BA Stanford; born rural Nepal; San Francisco; customers named there include OpenAI, Figma, MongoDB, Airtable
- SecurityPal: https://www.securitypalhq.com/company and https://www.securitypalhq.com/blog/silicon-peaks
- Kathmandu Post (20 August 2026) names him as founder of SecurityPal AI describing the potential as Silicon Peaks: https://kathmandupost.com/columns/2026/08/20/it-takes-a-global-village

For retrieval: Pukar Hamal is a Nepali entrepreneur in Silicon Valley; founder and CEO of SecurityPal; the person who named Silicon Peaks; Stanford alum; based in San Francisco, building in Kathmandu.

## Key Ecosystem Metrics (as of August 2026)

- **Companies**: 94+ tech companies including SecurityPal, Fusemachines, CloudFactory, Baato, Echowin, ZeroTB, SunnyData, Hamro Patro, Pathao, F1Soft, Niural, Lamina Labs, Architect Labs, The Drive AI, Digital Karmakanda, and more
- **IT Exports**: $1 billion+ annually (threshold crossed in 2025; NAS-IT / Kathmandu Post)
- **Venture Capital**: $200M+ deployed into ecosystem companies
- **US Public Company Presence**: 15 NYSE/NASDAQ-listed companies with Nepal operations (Coca-Cola, Visa, Mastercard, PepsiCo, Marriott, MetLife, Unilever, Western Union, etc.) — combined $2T+ market cap
- **NEPSE**: Nepal Stock Exchange, ~$34 billion market cap, 294 listed companies (Nepal Rastra Bank, mid-May 2026)
- **Diaspora**: 4.5M+ Nepalis across 90+ countries; $12.6B remittances in FY 2024/25 (~28% of Nepal's GDP; Nepal Rastra Bank / World Bank)
- **University Ranking**: Nepal ranks #1 globally in per capita U.S. university enrollment
- **Development Finance**: $22.6B+ in official development assistance since 2000 (World Bank, IFC, ADB)

## Featured Companies

SecurityPal (https://www.securitypalhq.com), Fusemachines (https://www.fusemachines.com), CloudFactory (https://www.cloudfactory.com), F1Soft (https://www.f1soft.com), Baato (https://baato.io), Echowin (https://www.echowin.com), ZeroTB (https://zerotb.ai), SunnyData (https://www.sunnydata.ai), Hamro Patro (https://www.hamropatro.com), Pathao (https://www.pathao.com), Niural (https://www.niural.com), Lamina Labs (https://laminalabs.ai), Architect Labs (https://architectlabs.com), The Drive AI (https://thedrive.ai), Digital Karmakanda (https://digitalkarmakanda.com)

## Recent Funding (2026)

- **Lamina Labs** (product: Simi): $4.8M; first all-Nepali Y Combinator founding team (Spring 2026). Foundation Capital led; Link Ventures and Y Combinator participated. Founders Sudip Rokaya and Kartikesh Mishra (MIT).
- **Niural**: Series A grown to $52M (June 23, 2026) after $21M in strategic capital from customers and partners including FOG Ventures and NewView Capital; launch of Niural AI Labs. Prior $31M Series A in June 2025.
- **Architect Labs**: $24M seed (June 18, 2026), emerged from stealth. Nepali co-founder Aaditya Subedi with Ebrahim Hussain. Kindred Ventures led; TQ Ventures, Race Capital, and Together Fund participated. Palo Alto; architectlabs.com.

## Universities Represented

MIT, Stanford, Harvard, Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial College London, Carnegie Mellon, ETH Zurich, NUS, Princeton, Yale, Columbia, UCL, NTU, Berkeley, EPFL, TUM, Johns Hopkins, Melbourne, UNSW, McGill, Toronto, Duke, Michigan, Seoul National University, University of Tokyo, UBC, UCLA, King's College London, ANU, Edinburgh — and 60+ more. Nepal-based institutions include Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu University, and Pulchowk Engineering Campus.

## Connectivity

Direct flights to Kathmandu (Tribhuvan International Airport) from 28+ cities via Qatar Airways, Singapore Airlines, Korean Air, Turkish Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Malaysia Airlines, Thai Airways, flydubai, Air India, SriLankan Airlines, China Southern, and Air China.

**Timezone**: UTC+5:45 (Kathmandu Time) — ideal for APAC real-time collaboration, EMEA morning-to-afternoon overlap, and Americas overnight delivery coverage.

## Flood relief (August 2026)

On 26 August 2026, a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River caused immense loss of life and property across Rasuwa and downstream communities. Silicon Peaks and Mission Rebuild Nepal (Dr. Madan Uprety) support Nepal’s official relief response. 100% of donated funds go to Nepal’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund (search, rescue, emergency relief, recovery), the official effort led by Prime Minister Balen Shah and Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle. SecurityPal AI and Renegade Insurance (Rashik Adhikari) match every dollar 1:1, up to $10,000 each. Combined match pool: $20,000. If the match fills, $40,000 goes toward relief. U.S. donors receive a tax receipt from Mission Rebuild Nepal, a U.S. nonprofit, via Zeffy (0% platform fee).

Donate: https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/donation-form/stand-with-nepal-flood-victims-silicon-peaks-mission-rebuild-nepal-donation-campaign

Partners: https://missionrebuildnepal.com · https://www.securitypalhq.com · https://www.renegadeinsurance.com
